sections.title: Final Instructions and Greetings
observations: In this section, Paul provides final instructions regarding the collection for the saints in Jerusalem. He emphasizes the importance of generosity and planning ahead for this collection, which reflects the unity of the church and the support of fellow believers in need.

Paul encourages the Corinthians to set aside a sum of money on the first day of the week, indicating a practice of regular giving. This highlights the principle of stewardship and the responsibility of believers to contribute to the needs of others.
The mention of sending the collected funds with trustworthy individuals underscores the importance of accountability in financial matters within the church.

sections.title: Travel Plans and Personal Remarks
observations: Paul shares his travel plans, indicating that he intends to visit the Corinthians after passing through Macedonia. This shows his desire for personal connection and encouragement among the believers.
He mentions Timothy and Apollos, urging the Corinthians to treat them with respect and hospitality. This reflects the importance of unity and support among church leaders and members.

sections.title: Exhortation to Stand Firm
observations: In this concluding section, Paul exhorts the Corinthians to be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, and be strong. This call to spiritual vigilance and strength is crucial for the church's health and growth.
Paul emphasizes love as the foundation of all actions, reminding the Corinthians that their efforts must be rooted in love for one another.

importantVerses.commentary: On the first day of the week, each of you is to put something aside and store it up, as he may prosper, so that there will be no collecting when I come.
Let all that you do be done in love.

questions: What does Paul's instruction about the collection reveal about the early church's understanding of generosity?
How can we apply Paul's exhortation to stand firm in our faith in today's context?
What role does love play in the actions and relationships within the church according to this chapter?
